questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes “SN2 reaction”?

options.label: A
options.text: A solvent that lacks acidic protons and solvates cations well while leaving nucleophiles naked and highly reactive, favoring SN2 pathways.

options.label: B
options.text: A concerted, bimolecular elimination reaction where a base removes a proton as the leaving group departs from an anti-periplanar conformation.

options.label: C
options.text: The required stereoelectronic geometry for E2 elimination where the beta-proton and leaving group are coplanar and separated by 180 degrees.

options.label: D
options.text: A concerted, bimolecular nucleophilic substitution reaction characterized by backside attack, second-order kinetics, and complete inversion of configuration.

questions.correct_answer: A concerted, bimolecular nucleophilic substitution reaction characterized by backside attack, second-order kinetics, and complete inversion of configuration.
questions.explanation: A accurate description of SN2 reaction is: A concerted, bimolecular nucleophilic substitution reaction characterized by backside attack, second-order kinetics, and complete inversion of configuration.
